judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's mathematical claims hold on independent recomputation: the chart in problem 1 reads 47,382 with the 7 worth 7,000; 40,000 divided by 4,000 is 10; 500,000+30,000+8,000+60+2 is 538,062; 46,315 < 46,351 at the tens place; 'two hundred nine thousand, forty' is 209,040; 8,921 < 80,912 < 80,921; 47,382 rounds to 47,000; the 5 in 350,842 is worth 50,000; 18,000 + 22,000 is 40,000 (verify.py's estimate type rounds each operand before evaluating, which is the procedure the worksheet teaches); and the judge's specific praise of the two-town item is exact - Ashford 34,650 and Belmont 34,509 both round to 35,000 while 34,650 > 34,509. Two things the judge did not check contradict the perfect 32/32. First, verify.json tags problems 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10 with '2.NBT.A', a Grade 2 place-value standard limited to numbers under 1,000, and the answer key prints '2.NBT.A - problems 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10' directly beneath 'Level: Grades 4-5'; the task contract names 4.NBT.A / 5.NBT.A and references/standards-map.md carries the correct row. Second, the Quick Answers bank prints '4. ---' and '10. 35000, ---': both comparison relations were verified ('<' and '>') but render as the em dash the bank documents as meaning 'manual, see solution'.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 10 is the best-designed item on the sheet: (a) rounds Ashford to 35,000, then (b) makes the student notice that rounding cannot answer 'which town has more', and the key closes with 'Two numbers can round to the same thousand and still be 141 apart - an estimate is never a substitute for a comparison.' Keep the pattern of a final item that exposes the limit of the method the sheet just taught.

Problem 3 omits the hundreds place from the expanded form (500,000 + 30,000 + 8,000 + 60 + 2) and the key names the consequence exactly: 'writing 53,862 drops the hundreds place and shrinks the number by a factor of ten.' The zero-as-placeholder idea is taught by the numbers chosen, not by an instruction.

The study guide's closing watch-out reuses the worksheet's own hardest numbers (34,650 and 34,509 both round to 35,000), so the reference page and the practice page reinforce one idea rather than two unrelated ones.

root_causes.description: scripts/verify.py documents 'standard' as a reporting tag that never gates, while scripts/render_quick_answers.curriculum_block prints those same tags verbatim on the answer key beneath the grade level. Nothing checks a tag against the sheet's band, so an off-grade code chosen during generation reaches the reader unchallenged - the exact failure references/standards-map.md warns about in its own preamble.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-101/verify.json: eight of the ten problems declare "standard": "2.NBT.A"
evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-101/answer_key.pdf page 1 prints 'Level: Grades 4-5 ...' immediately above '2.NBT.A - problems 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10'
references/standards-map.md has the correct row 'Place value & powers of ten (gr 4-5) | 4.NBT.A.1-A.3 / 5.NBT.A.1-A.2', and the packet's task contract declares standard_refs '4.NBT.A / 5.NBT.A'

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies every string expected value; sympify('<') raises SympifyError and the handler falls through to the '---' placeholder that the module's own docstring reserves for manual-only ids. A verified comparison answer is therefore presented to the grader as if it had no machine-checked value.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-101/verify.json id 4 expects '<' and the second id 10 entry expects '>'
scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt(): the str branch returns '---' on SympifyError

improvements.title: Gate the printed CCSS tags against the sheet's declared grade band
improvements.proposed_change: verify.py documents 'standard' as a reporting tag that never gates, while render_quick_answers.curriculum_block prints those same tags verbatim on the answer key directly beneath the grade level. Add a gate that reads the leading grade of each declared code and fails when a tag sits more than one grade below the sheet's declared band, naming the correct row from references/standards-map.md in the failure message. Restate in the standards map that the fix for a missing topic is to add the row with the real code, never to borrow the nearest lower-grade domain.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_curriculum_eval_suite.py (or a new standards gate test) that runs the tag gate over a verify JSON declaring a Grades 4-5 place-value sheet with "standard": "2.NBT.A". The gate must exit non-zero and name the 4.NBT.A / 5.NBT.A row; retagging to 4.NBT.A.2 must exit 0. Today no gate reads the tag at all, so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The Curriculum block stops telling a parent or teacher that a Grade 4-5 or Grade 6-7 packet covers a Grade 2 or Grade 3 standard, which is the one place on the packet an adult looks to place the work in a curriculum.
improvements.risk: Deliberate below-band review content would trip the gate, so allow an explicit per-problem acknowledgement that a prior-grade standard is intended.

improvements.title: Stop pushing relation symbols and interval keywords through sympify in the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: render_quick_answers._fmt calls sympy.sympify on every string 'expected' and renders whatever comes back. Two vocabularies are not expressions and must be handled before that call. First, relation strings ('<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=') from compare problems raise SympifyError and degrade to the '---' the module documents as meaning 'manual, see solution', so a verified answer is advertised as unavailable. Second, the endpoint and closure triple of an inequality problem contains the literal 'open', which sympify resolves to the Python builtin open() and sympy.latex renders as \mathtt{\text{<built-in function open>}}. Render relations verbatim as math, render an inequality triple as the solution the student writes (x < -3) or as standard interval notation, never sympify the literals open/closed/oo/-oo, and make a sympify result that is not a SymPy object a hard error rather than a rendered repr.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_render_quick_answers.py, render a bank from a verify JSON containing {"id": 4, "type": "compare", "order": "relation", "expected": "<"} and assert the entry for problem 4 renders '$<$' and is not '---'. The assertion fails on today's _fmt, which returns '---', and passes once relation strings bypass sympify.
improvements.expected_impact: The at-a-glance grading bank stops printing Python internals into a teacher-facing PDF and stops blanking out every comparison answer on comparison-heavy sheets, where today it can be more than half empty.
improvements.risk: Low. The change is confined to one formatting helper, and the fixture-locked invariant that bank entries stay plain text outside \ans and \boxed is untouched.

case_summary: A genuinely strong Grades 4-5 place-value packet. All ten problems and both parts of problems 1 and 10 are mathematically correct and independently reconfirmed, the place-value charts and the 'which thousands does it sit between' table are tied to notation as the concept-models prompt asks, every printed answer slot has a verify entry (twelve entries for ten problems), and the study guide gives four rules, four worked examples and four distinct try-its. Two defects sit under the 32/32: the answer key's Curriculum block advertises a Grades 4-5 sheet as covering the Grade 2 standard 2.NBT.A, and the Quick Answers bank drops both verified comparison answers to an em dash. Neither touches the mathematics, but the first misinforms the adult reader and the second removes two of ten answers from the fast-grading column.
